script: You are Gustav Krukenberg, and Berlin just handed you soldiers who are not even German. Three hundred Frenchmen, all that is left of an SS division that once had eleven thousand men in its ranks. The Red Army is two streets from the bunker, and Hitler is underground with a pistol he has not used yet. You put the French where the fighting is worst, because they are the only unit left still willing to die for a country that is not theirs. Here's the part nobody mentions. On April 28th your men destroy sixty-two Soviet tanks in a single day, more than any German unit still standing that week. France will call every one of them a traitor for it. Most of your men get sentenced to death before the guns even go cold, for defending a war that was never their war and a man who never once trusted them. You survive the bunker. You do not survive France. Hitler kills himself on April 30th, and the fighting goes on for two more days, because nobody told the men still holding his door. Three hundred foreigners were the last men standing between the Red Army and Adolf Hitler's door.

title: 300 Frenchmen Died Defending Hitler. Why Did They Do It?
description:
By the last week of the war, Hitler's own army had almost nothing left — except three hundred French volunteers nobody in Germany trusted. They held the line around his bunker until the guns went silent, then went home to a country that wanted to execute them for it.

Who were they really dying for, at that point?
